ratings_why.fun: A sawtooth curve whose peaks climb each cycle through The Moon-Scour, with three real builds; the dark turns still cost Health before Tier 5.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7: no tribe today has a visible clock that wipes every buff, so each buy becomes a shelf-life call and doubling runs safely under the reset.

verdict_why: Dame Waxwell's trigger order with Chalk-Cutter and The Moon-Scour is unstated and changes the Full Moon spike by two to four times.

points.text: Say how Dame Waxwell's second trigger resolves: all Full Moon effects once and then all again (Scour, Cutter, Scour, Cutter), or each twice in place. The two readings differ by two to four times on the spike.

The first New Moon on turn 4 wipes the early buffs, and the only dark-turn holder is Dusk-Runner at Tier 5. A small Tier 2 or 3 unit that is stronger on New and Waxing fights would smooth the early climb.
Charm-Pedlar pays almost nothing before turn 8. It could also pay 1 gold on Full Moons, so the Fast Moon build has early economy.
In a pure Hare board, Sister Silverpenny copying your biggest Hare is weak. She could copy the biggest Hare's light too, so she earns her slot without another tribe.

standouts.why: Chalk-Cutter turns seating into the puzzle: a safe multiplier because the light always goes out.
Old Wat is the tribe's own loophole, a Jack who keeps what the coven loses.
The Moon-Scour's counter makes each cycle's peak higher, which gives the late game a shape to chase.

weakest.why: Charm-Pedlar has little lost light to cash early and only pays every fourth turn at normal speed.
Sister Silverpenny depends on other tribes and does little in a pure Hare board.
Dusk-Runner's +8/+8 is well under a Tier 5 in-fight target; it holds the dark turns but barely.

flags.note: Order of the doubled Full Moon triggers against Chalk-Cutter and The Moon-Scour is not stated.
Mother Meikle Care banks half of a multiplied cycle as permanent stats, and the amount climbs each cycle, faster with a fast Moon.
Golden Chalk-Cutter (triple) under golden Dame Waxwell (three triggers) multiplies light up to 27 times in one Full Moon.
Ringside Bookie with Moon-Caller sells lit Hares for gold and Waxes into the next Full Moon; bounded at 3 extra gold a Hare, but worth a sim.
